# CI/CD

Prevents: a pipeline that runs untrusted code with your deploy credentials, and
a production change nobody could undo.

CI files are **generated** — edit `harness.config.yaml`, then `make ci-gen`.
Hand-edits are overwritten and CI fails on the drift.

## Credentials

- **Never copy action versions from vendor tutorials.** They run two to three
  majors behind. Resolve current ones and pin to a commit SHA — `make pin-actions`.
- **Keyless wherever the provider supports it.** GCP, AWS and Azure all accept
  GitHub OIDC. Any job authenticating to one declares
  `permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write }` — without `id-token` there
  is no OIDC token and the only alternative is a long-lived key.
- A federation pool **always** carries an attribute condition, bound to
  `repository_id` / `repository_owner_id`. A pool without one can be entered by
  any repository on GitHub. Do not match on a name-parsed `sub` — subjects are
  moving to immutable ID-embedded form and name-based matches break on rename.
- Vercel and Supabase have **no keyless path**. Their tokens are long-lived, so
  they live in a protected *environment* secret, never a repo secret —
  environment secrets stay unreadable until the protection rule passes.

## Untrusted input

- **Never pair `pull_request_target` with a checkout of fork code.** That is
  running an outsider's code with your elevated token. `actions/checkout` v7
  refuses by default; if you ever reach for `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout`, write
  down why in the same commit.
- Branch names, PR bodies and issue titles reach a script through `env:`, never
  through direct `${{ }}` interpolation into a command line.

## Production

- Every production job references a CI `environment:`. Required reviewers are
  configured in repo settings and **cannot be expressed in YAML** — the
  generator prints the instruction and nothing here can verify it was done.
- **Deploy and cutover are separate steps** where the platform allows it
  (`--no-traffic --tag`, `--prod --skip-domain`), with the gate between them.
- Anything mutating production data or schema runs its dry run first, and the
  two steps sit either side of the approval.
- Tag artifacts by commit SHA. Never `latest` — a mutable tag makes it
  impossible to say what is running or to reproduce a rollback.
- If the platform has its own Git integration and you also deploy from CI,
  **turn one off.** Two pipelines racing to deploy the same commit is a bad day.

## Know what cannot be undone

| Platform | Rollback |
|---|---|
| Cloud Run | Real. Revisions immutable, traffic is a pointer, seconds. |
| Vercel | `promote` an earlier deployment. |
| **Supabase migrations** | **None.** No down migrations, no revert. Recovery is restore-from-backup plus a compensating forward migration. |

An agent may prepare a production deploy. It may not run one unless a person
asked in that turn.
